runtimeRule: A class requires a live register row, a real video, and a current admitted class learning record.

records.learningObjective: Distinguish an AI app from the model and other services it can use, trace what becomes working context, and choose what needs verification.
records.prerequisite: No prior AI knowledge; learner can open one conversational AI product.
records.mentalModel: The app coordinates instructions, conversation context and optional capabilities such as files, search or other tools; a model processes the supplied context and produces or helps select the next output or action.
adjacentDistinctions: a model capability versus a product feature or account entitlement
misconceptions: The app and the model are the same thing.
Conversational AI never searches or uses tools.
Anything an assistant says came from a verified source.
A new chat always means the product has no other memory or connected data.

modality.narration: Build the app-model-tools-context distinction in that order and state uncertainty before the demonstration.
modality.images: Use a labelled layer diagram and real, date-stamped interface captures; every image must match the narration at that moment.
modality.animation: Animate only the flow of a request, optional tool result and response. Do not use decorative character motion as a substitute for the mechanism.
modality.demonstration: Run one task first without search and then with visible search/citations, naming what changed and what still requires checking.
modality.captions: Caption the final approved narration verbatim and identify meaningful interface states without relying on colour alone.

analogy.text: Think of the app as a studio, the model as one performer, and tools as equipment the studio may make available.
analogy.limit: A model is not a person, and product orchestration is not literally a studio; use the analogy only to separate layers.

uncertainty: Product features, defaults, model names and account entitlements change.
Vendors use overlapping terms for models, assistants, apps, tools, memory and connectors.

records.objective: Check whether the learner can apply the app-model-tools-context distinction and choose an appropriate verification action.

questions.prompt: You upload a PDF in an AI app and ask for a summary. Which description is most accurate?
options: The app supplies the file and instructions as working context for a model to process.
The model permanently learns the whole PDF for every future user.
Uploading proves every statement in the PDF is true.
questions.answer: The app supplies the file and instructions as working context for a model to process.
questions.explanation: The product handles the file and passes usable information to the model. That does not make the file true or permanently retrain the model.
questions.misconception: File upload means permanent training or automatic verification.
questions.reviewAction: Return to the request-flow diagram and name the app, context and model layers.

questions.prompt: An answer includes clickable web citations. What changed?
options: The product used a search or retrieval capability and supplied results to the answering flow.
The model became incapable of generating text.
Every cited claim is now guaranteed correct.
questions.answer: The product used a search or retrieval capability and supplied results to the answering flow.
questions.explanation: Search can add current source material, but the learner must still inspect whether each source supports the claim.
questions.reviewAction: Open one citation and compare the source with the sentence it is meant to support.

questions.prompt: Two products use similarly named models but show different buttons and limits. Why can that happen?
options: Product features, connected tools and account entitlements can differ from the underlying model.
A model name determines every part of an app.
One of the products must be fake.
questions.answer: Product features, connected tools and account entitlements can differ from the underlying model.
questions.explanation: The model is one layer. The app controls interface, tool access, policies, limits and account features.
questions.misconception: Model capability and product availability are identical.
questions.reviewAction: Name one feature controlled by the app rather than the model alone.

questions.prompt: A new chat remembers a preference. What is the safest conclusion?
options: The product may have a memory or instruction feature; check its controls and scope.
The model secretly reads every file on the device.
New chats can never receive information from product features.
questions.answer: The product may have a memory or instruction feature; check its controls and scope.
questions.explanation: A new conversation can still receive saved instructions or memory depending on the product and settings.
questions.misconception: New chat always means no persisted product context.
questions.reviewAction: Find the product's official memory or privacy controls before making a claim.

questions.prompt: Which task most clearly needs verification after an assistant answers?
options: Summarising a current eligibility rule that affects an application.
Brainstorming playful names for a private playlist.
Changing a paragraph from formal to friendly.
questions.answer: Summarising a current eligibility rule that affects an application.
questions.explanation: The rule is current and consequential. Check the responsible authority's live source rather than trusting fluent wording.
questions.misconception: A confident answer is enough evidence for a current consequential fact.
questions.reviewAction: Identify the authority, date and exact claim that must be checked.
